profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary:
● Generalist software engineer
● Interests
    ○ Systems problems related to the interactions among hardware, operating systems, compilers, and applications
    ○ Compile-time tools, runtime daemons, or frameworks
    ○ Debugging and code enhancement w.r.t language/OS/HW internals and concurrency
    ○ End impact of technologies and supportive team dynamics
● Research background in static analysis, compilers, computer architecture, and EDA
● Programming languages: Modern C++, Rust, Python

I appreciate the beauty of abstraction; that’s what enables us to use software to solve real-world problems.

Resume at https://drive.google.com/file/d/14rXDxTBJz5RwsKNU40SxzbpxxeVdSgti/view?usp=sharing

company.name: Mercedes-Benz Research & Development North America, Inc.

positions.title: Member of Technical Staff
positions.description:
Networking, SAN, iSCSI in FlashArray.
- Achieved over 70x scaling of a performance-statistics reporting service in the system
- Async programming, concurrency, multithreading, kernel module
- C++, Python

positions.title: Senior R&D Engineer I
positions.description:
Physical synthesis optimization in Fusion Compiler.
- Optimization flow setup
- Runtime analysis and optimization
- Nondeterminism resolution

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Researched static program analysis and code transformation for performance optimization on GPUs, multi-cores, or embedded microprocessors with software-managed memory hierarchies.  
. Research topics included:
- Static performance modeling and estimation of CUDA applications 
- Inserting branch-hint instructions for Cell BE with software branch hinting mechanism. 
- Static worst-case execution time (WCET) analysis 
- Compiler optimization techniques for software-managed on-chip memories.

Thesis title: WCET-Aware Scratchpad Memory Management for Hard Real-time Systems

positions.title: Visiting Research Intern
positions.description:
Involved in the DOE-supported XStack research project on exascale computing at Intel Federal. 
- Implemented transformation passes in LLVM for managing scratchpad memories.

positions.title: Visiting Student Researcher
positions.description:
Researched compiler support for the PRET architecture, specialized for hard real-time systems.
- Developed a static code analysis technique to calculate the WCET.
- Developed linear-programming-based optimal techniques and heuristic algorithms to help compiler backend decide memory allocation schemes for dynamically loading instructions onto on-chip scratchpad.

positions.title: Research Co-op
positions.description:
Developed worst-case execution time (WCET) analysis and explored the benefit of using new processor architecture in the powertrain control systems. 
- Developed optimal memory allocation techniques along with optimizing heuristics.
- Achieved 65% on average and up to 70% WCET reduction in power train control applications.
